episodes.181229: Storms across the Gila mountain range drifted north over western New Mexico through outflow boundaries. This allowed a decaying thunderstorm over Grants and a developing thunderstorm over Farmington to produce dry microbursts at the respective airport observing sites.
episodes.181271: A supercell developed during the morning and tracked across east central Minnesota. This storm produced quarter to golfball size hail.
episodes.181362: A weak disturbance interacted with mid-level moisture and modest shear to bring scattered strong thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening of the 27th.
episodes.181407: A line of showers and thunderstorms with strong outflow winds moved across south-central and southeast Wyoming during the afternoon on the 26th.
episodes.181435: A shortwave tracked through the eastern Great Lakes early on the morning of July 27th and moved into New England by the afternoon hours while a stalled boundary draped remained draped across the area.  This allowed for a favorable set-up for rotating storms due to very high low level helicity values.  A discrete supercell formed in Cheshire County bringing a relatively long tracked tornado and large hail.  The storm weakened with the tornado lifting before it briefly strengthened again over the Manchester area bringing with straight line wind damage.
episodes.181593: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front drifting southward towards central Pennsylvania. A narrow band of sub-severe storms developed across northern PA, closer to the front, with a few discrete cells develop across southern PA.  One of these discreet southern cells was able to produce sporadic wind damage in Lancaster County.
episodes.181613: A complex of thunderstorms crossing Lake Erie pushed across western New York during the evening hours. The storms produced sporadic wind damage over western New York before weakening as they tracked farther east.
episodes.181634: A convective system kicked off multiple rounds of thunderstorms in Sullivan County in New York. These severe storms had damaging wind gusts. There were a few reports of trees down with some trees catching on fire after landing on live utility wires.
episodes.181635: A mesoscale convective system brought a line of thunderstorms through Northeastern Pennsylvania. These storms contained damaging wind gusts. There were multiple reports of trees and wires down.
episodes.181695: Strong to severe thunderstorms associated with a shortwave trough and cold front developed and moved over parts of eastern New York during the afternoon and evening hours on July 27th resulting in numerous reports of downed trees and wires across the region.
episodes.181701: Strong to severe thunderstorms associated with a shortwave trough and cold front developed and moved over parts of northwestern Connecticut during the afternoon and evening hours on July 27th resulting in multiple reports of downed trees and wires across the area.
episodes.181702: Strong to severe thunderstorms associated with a shortwave trough and cold front developed and moved over parts of western Massachusetts during the afternoon and evening hours on July 27th resulting in numerous reports of downed trees and wires across the area.
episodes.181756: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front tracking through western Wisconsin during the late afternoon hours on Thursday (7/27).  The thunderstorms tracked through central and north-central Wisconsin during the early evening hours.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds, hail up to half dollar size and a tornado.
episodes.181896: A weak trough spawned several severe thunderstorms over the far eastern West Virginia panhandle, extreme northern Virginia, and north-central Maryland.
episodes.181897: A weak trough spawned several severe thunderstorms over the far eastern West Virginia panhandle, extreme northern Virginia, and north-central Maryland.
episodes.181898: A weak trough spawned several severe thunderstorms over the far eastern West Virginia panhandle, extreme northern Virginia, and north-central Maryland.
episodes.181944: A weak trough spawned several thunderstorms, one of which produced localized gale-force wind gusts over the upper tidal Potomac River.
episodes.182072: Seabreeze thunderstorm over Pinellas County produces strong marine wind gust.
episodes.182205: A thunderstorm briefly became severe over portions of southwestern South Dakota, producing some wind gusts over 60 mph.
episodes.182352: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the evening hours in a warm and humid airmass. The thunderstorms persisted into the overnight hours.
episodes.182510: The last few days of July featured hot and muggy conditions alongside strong to severe thunderstorms. Only one storm proved to be severe on July 27th, passing through Gallia County in the afternoon and causing downed trees. More widespread storms took place across southeast Ohio on the 28th, with an increase in areas observing tree and power line damage as a result of the strong winds passing through. Once storms crossed the Ohio River each day, the risk for severe weather concluded.
episodes.182705: The final few days of July featured very hot and muggy weather across West Virginia. During peak heating hours, the atmosphere became conducive for afternoon showers and thunderstorms. Mainly isolated storm reports occurred on July 27th and 29th, while widespread damage took place on the 28th. ||On that particular day, hot temperatures and ample low level moisture yielded a convective line of activity across Ohio and Kentucky that eventually crossed into West Virginia. Strong winds accompanying the line resulted in a swath of downed trees and power lines starting in Wood County shortly before 3 PM and then spreading eastward through the bulk of central and southeastern West Virginia. ||At the Charleston Yeager International Airport, a 62 mile per hour wind gust was measured. Around that time, multiple areas of downed trees and power lines were observed in and around downtown Charleston. Storms eventually crossed out of the forecast area by the early evening.||While damaging wind gusts were the main issues during this stretch of unsettled weather, there was one instance of flash flooding on July 27th from activity passing over the western portions of Kanawha County. This led to high water reports in a few spots in and around Cross Lanes.
episodes.182713: A potent mid level shortwave moved in from the Great Lakes bringing widespread wind damage.
episodes.182714: A potent mid level shortwave moved in from the Great Lakes bringing widespread wind damage.
episodes.182722: A potent mid level shortwave moved in from the Great Lakes bringing widespread wind damage.
episodes.182965: Prolonged hot and humid conditions coupled with dry mid-levels in the atmosphere, led to extreme amounts of mixed-layer convective available potential energy (MLCAPE). The existence of deep layer shear allowed for numerous strong updrafts to develop across East Central MN with the primary hazard being hail in the afternoon hours. Later that evening in Southwestern MN, a surface boundary would converge on a cold pool which then would produce a line of thunderstorms capable of producing damaging wind gusts.||Hail measurements ranged between penny (0.75 inch) to Hen-Egg (2.0 inch) size. The highest measured hail was reported in the city of Morgan, MN or 13 miles SE of Redwood Falls located in Redwood County. ||Strong winds uprooted trees, broke large tree branches across much of the region affected by these storms. The areas with the most damage occurred in Chisago County as well as a line from Nicollet to Waseca Counties. The strongest gust (57 mph) was recorded at 11:56 PM at the Mankato Regional Airport.
episodes.182966: Prolonged hot and humid conditions coupled with dry mid-levels in the atmosphere, led to extreme amounts of mixed-layer convective available potential energy (MLCAPE). The existence of deep layer shear allowed for numerous strong updrafts to develop across parts of Western WI with the primary hazards being large hail and damaging winds in the afternoon and early evening hours. ||Hail measurements ranged between nickel (0.88 inch) to tea-cup (3.0 inch) size. The largest measured hail was reported 2.5 miles north of Bloomer or 5 miles NW of Chippewa Falls, WI. ||Strong winds uprooted trees, broke large tree branches across, and brought down powerlines across much of the region affected by these storms. The areas with the most wind damage occurred along a line from Polk to Rusk Counties. Strongest wind gusts were estimated to be at least 50 knots or 57 mph.
episodes.183163: Severe thunderstorms caused large hail up to ping pong ball sized and damaging wind gusts in Northwestern Minnesota.
episodes.183184: A tropical wave moving over South Florida provided a moisture-rich environment for widespread showers and thunderstorms to develop on the afternoon of July 27th.
episodes.183185: A tropical wave moving over South Florida provided an environment for widespread showers and thunderstorms with high rainfall rates on the afternoon and evening of July 27th. Several of these showers and storms were pinned along the sea breeze and very slow-moving, primarily across Broward County.
episodes.183214: A cold front moving across a moist and unstable airmass generated severe thunderstorms over mainly the west half of Upper Michigan during the evening of the 27th.
episodes.183263: The passage of a surface trough and cold front through an unstable air mass led to the development of strong to severe thunderstorms over Lake Superior on the 27th.
episodes.183279: An area of low pressure and associated cold front brought thunderstorms to central and north central South Dakota during the evening hours on July 26th. Golf ball to tennis ball size hail broke multiple windows and caused damage to property seven miles south-southeast of Chantier Creek Recreation area.
episodes.183364: A line of thunderstorms formed over northern Ohio during the evening of July 26th and raced across southwest Pennsylvania to the north of Pittsburgh, supported by a shortwave trough.  Many wind damage reports were received in the vicinity of the I-80 corridor, with isolated flash flooding as well.
episodes.183395: Warm and humid conditions developed across northeastern Minnesota on the 27th ahead of a frontal boundary that stalled out across the region. Storms developed during the afternoon hours and were prolific hail producers and they moved through. Multiple reports of hail to the size of tennis balls were received. A few areas of wind damage were reported as well, primarily in the Duluth area.
episodes.183397: Warm and humid conditions developed across northeastern Minnesota on the 27th ahead of a frontal boundary that stalled out across the region. Storms were primarily hail producers across northeastern Minnesota but transitioned to more of a wind threat as they grew upscale across northwestern Wisconsin. Numerous reports of trees and powerlines downed were received across the area with some flash flooding occurring later in the afternoon as well in areas that saw multiple rounds of storms.
episodes.183401: Warm and humid conditions developed across northeastern Minnesota on the 27th ahead of a frontal boundary that stalled out across the region. Storms were primarily hail producers across northeastern Minnesota but transitioned to more of a wind threat as they grew upscale across western Lake Superior and northwestern Wisconsin. A wind gust of 53 mph was recorded at the ferry dock in LaPointe on Madison Island.
episodes.183420: With the subtropical high pressure situated across central New Mexico, a southeasterly wind flow was established across Arizona. Thunderstorm activity developed across portions of southeast AZ during the afternoon hours. MLCAPE between 500-1000 J/KG as well as Downdraft CAPE near 2000 J/KG aided in creating a favorable environment for the thunderstorm activity to result in strong downburst winds. The first thunderstorm activity to develop across portions of southeast AZ resulted in the development of a strong outflow boundary, responsible for dense blowing dust conditions across Pinal and southern Maricopa Counties as well as sparking additional storms that affected portions of the Phoenix metro area. With the thunderstorms that moved across the Phoenix metro area, there were several reports of tree damage as well as structural damage to several homes.
episodes.183439: A small scale thunderstorm system brought a line of heavy rain-producing thunderstorms through Northeastern Pennsylvania. These storms contained torrential rainfall which led to isolated areas of flooding.
episodes.183466: Scattered supercells across southwest Nebraska resulted in large hail and strong winds during the late afternoon and early evening hours of July 26.
episodes.183522: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed near I-10 in Vicksburg Junction in southwest Arizona during the late afternoon hours on the 27th, resulting in multiple tractor trailers being blown over along I-10 between mile posts 41-47. The environment the thunderstorm developed under was characterized by MLCAPE of approximately 500 J/KG along with DCAPE of approximately 2000 J/KG, more than sufficient to result in strong downburst winds.
episodes.183529: Sufficient moisture continued to flow through the region in late July, leading to daytime convection most days. This convection was occasionally strong to severe, yielding localized strong wind gusts in addition to flash flooding.
episodes.183805: Multiple rounds of convection occurred. The first round of storms intensified arriving into northern Indiana and southern Michigan, resulting in wind damage along and north of US 6. Another round of damaging winds and heavy rainfall occurred across southern Lower Michigan later in the day. Storms continued to back build into the evening. Locally heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches occurred across southern Lower Michigan.
episodes.183809: Storms developed along a stalled frontal boundary on the evening of July 28th. These storms developed in clusters and were slow moving with heavy rain. They also produced sporadic wind damage across northwest Indiana. An EF0 tornado also occurred in Cass County.
episodes.183865: A tropical wave moving through South Florida triggered numerous showers and thunderstorms over the area and adjacent waters.
episodes.183875: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west from Cochise and Santa Cruz across Pima and Pinal counties during the afternoon and evening.  Thunderstorm winds produced a dust storm in Pinal County.
episodes.183876: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across Greenlee, Graham, Cochise, Santa Cruz and eastern Pima counties during the afternoon and evening. A few severe wind gusts occurred but no damage was reported.
episodes.183918: A cluster of storms developed off the Front Range moving east across the Eastern Colorado plains. The storms moved into Yuma County during the early evening hours producing thunderstorm wind gusts of 45 to 64 mph. The strongest gusts were observed near the community of Heartstrong and the city of Wray.
episodes.183928: A linear cluster of storms developed off the Front Range moving east across Northwest Kansas during the evening hours. The storms produced thunderstorm wind gusts up to 100 mph as they moved through, with the strongest gusts reported in the town of McDonald in Rawlins County. Damage occurred primarily to trees in portions of Cheyenne and Rawlins counties with additional damage to powerlines, campers, and structures. The thunderstorm wind gusts and the outflow of the storm also created dust storm conditions with visibilities of one-quarter mile or less observed in Cheyenne, Sherman, and Rawlins counties. Blowing dust with visibility reductions of three to five miles were also observed near the cities of Colby and Oakley.
episodes.183961: Deep tropical moisture surging northward in confluent lower tropospheric flow enhanced by the presence of a tropical upper tropospheric tutt (TUTT) cell over western Cuba supported scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms across the eastern Straits of Florida through Florida Bay.
episodes.183973: Isolated gale-force wind gusts associated with scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred over the coastal waters of the Middle and Upper Florida Keys as a tropical wave moved west through the area.
episodes.184004: A cold front moved across central Wyoming on July 26th and brought showers and thunderstorms that brought strong to damaging winds for portions of Fremont and Natrona Counties. The most intense storm occurred in Fremont County. There were numerous wind gusts over 58 mph and some gusts as high as 74 mph. Numerous limbs and trees were downed on the west side of Riverton, including at the Riverton Country Club. Wind gusts as high as 68 mph occurred in Natrona County as well as the line of thunderstorms moved eastward.
episodes.184096: Pop-up showers and thunderstorms developed in a very hot and humid airmass. A few storms produced damaging wind gusts across parts of Pennsylvania.
episodes.184156: A shortwave trough moved through aloft as a broken line of severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough. The severe storms produced damaging winds across southeastern NY.
episodes.184157: A shortwave trough moved through aloft as a broken line of severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough. The severe storms produced damaging winds across southern CT.
episodes.184159: A shortwave trough moved through aloft as a broken line of severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough. The severe storms produced damaging winds across the waters.
episodes.184279: Large hail reported near Soda Springs.
episodes.184402: Scattered thunderstorms associated with a surface trough of low pressure produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.185769: A surface low moved northeastward from central Lower MI to Georgian Bay during the early afternoon through late evening of the 26th. Simultaneously, the attendant warm front moved northeastward from southeastern Lower MI, western and central Lake Erie, and far-eastern OH to the Upper Saint Lawrence River Valley and far-northern NY. Within the warm sector, multiple lines and clusters of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally eastward across northern OH, in vicinity of a surface trough axis, and generated scattered straight-line convective wind damage, a measured severe convective wind gust, and an instance of severe hail. These storms encountered moderate to strong effective bulk shear and primarily moderate to strong MUCAPE.

A National Weather Service storm survey found that a tornado touched down near Base Hill Road in North Swanzey in Cheshire County and briefly lifted before touching down again near Route 101 near the Keene/Marlboro line. A few spotters viewed a rotating wall cloud and funnel as it moved near this location.  EF-1 damage was found in Marlboro due to damage to soft and hardwood trees along with some trees falling into parked vehicles. The tornado then intermittently skipped eastward nearly right along Route 101 downing hundreds of trees along the way but no structures were damaged, before arriving in Dublin.  It is there where trees fell on cars and buildings, ripped siding and shingles off of structures, broke windows, and knocked down several hundreds of large healthy trees. The tornado then lifted for good before reaching the intersection of Route 101 and Monument Road in Dublin.  Overall an estimated amount of around 1000 trees were uprooted or snapped.  5 buildings were partial damages, along with damage to small out buildings, some boats and a few parked vehicles.
